messages:
sam: Quick sync: runtime/control-plane contract for fallbacks and reattachment. We keep having ambiguous behavior when a runtime loses a claim and the control plane routes to fallback variants. Need clear rules: when substitution is allowed, who authorizes it, and how we surface it to apps.
vijay: Agreed. Key questions: can runtime autonomously serve a compatible quantized variant? Or must control plane pre-authorize per-claim?
elaine: My vote: control plane must express an allowed_fallbacks whitelist in the claim token. Runtime MAY serve any fallback from that list without extra auth. Runtime MUST NOT pick unknown variants.
morris: operationally, allow two fallback modes: soft_fallback (serve fallback but mark responses degraded) and hard_block (reject until control plane rebinds). Which to default to per-mode?
sam: Proposed defaults: hosted=soft_fallback, dedicated=hard_block, private=tenant-configurable (customer chooses). Rationale: hosted tolerates slight quality drop to avoid downtime; dedicated customers expect strict pinning.
vijay: We should encode fallback_quality_hint in token so SDKs can surface quality tradeoff to end-users. Example token claim payload snippet: 
```
{"sub":"rt-23","mode":"hosted","pin":"m-large@sha256:abcd","allowed_fallbacks":["m-large:quant-v2"],"fallback_policy":"soft","exp":1955560959}
```
elaine: Also need streaming-level signals. If runtime emits fallback mid-stream include an event: 
```
{"event":"fallback_in_use","fallback":"m-large:quant-v2","reason":"PREEMPT","hint":"quality:reduced"}
```
morris: For cache semantics: if fallback is used because of PREEMPT, we should avoid invalidating top-level model cache to speed reattach. But if fallback due to AUTHZ or COMPROMISE -> purge caches. So include cache_action: preserve|purge in the event.
sam: Circuit-breaker behavior: control plane should limit number of fallbacks per region per minute. If too many fallbacks occur, mark the model variant as degraded and route new requests to fallback pool proactively. Emit metric: fallback_spike{model,region}.
vijay: One tricky area: autonomous runtime substitutions for private deployments where customer policies might disallow: require delegated_claim issuer to include a field allow_runtime_subst=true. If absent, runtime must not substitute.
elaine: Observability: emit structured logs/events for claim lifecycle transitions: claim_issued, claim_renewed, claim_missed, claim_evicted, fallback_started, fallback_stopped. Each event must include mode, tenant_id, runtime_id, model_pin, and reason. Example line: 
```
{"ts":1955560001,"evt":"claim_evicted","mode":"dedicated","tenant":"acct-12","runtime":"rt-23","pin":"m-large@sha256:abcd","reason":"CAPACITY"}
```
morris: For SDK UX: when a response is served from fallback, include header `X-RW-Fallback: true` and `X-RW-Fallback-Variant: m-large:quant-v2` plus `X-RW-Fallback-Quality: reduced`. For streaming also emit the fallback event.
sam: Reattach strategy: add hot_reattach window and randomized backoff to avoid stampedes. Proposed defaults: hosted hot_reattach=180s, dedicated=60s, private=600s. Reattach clients should jitter and use leaky-bucket admission.
vijay: Billing implications: if fallback variant is cheaper (quantized), show `X-RW-Unit-Multiplier` indicating cost multiplier to billing layer. Example: `X-RW-Unit-Multiplier: 0.25`. This helps downstream cost attribution.
elaine: Security: token must pin model and include capabilities. Example claim JWT snippet: 
```
{"sub":"runtime-abc","mode":"dedicated","pin":"m-large@sha256:abcd","cap":["kvcache","streaming"],"allowed_fallbacks":["m-large:quant-v2"],"exp":1955560959}
```
morris: Private runtimes: if control plane unreachable, runtime can operate in offline_allowed mode if claim had offline_until timestamp. Runtime must record local audit journal `/var/lib/redwood/offline-claims` and POST on reconnect.
sam: Testing/rollout: probe-first for hosted/dedicated — control plane validates runtime supports declared substitution before enabling. For private: optimistic but require explicit tenant opt-in for runtime substitution.
vijay: Alerting: fire `fallback_rate_alert` when fallback percent > 0.5% p1 or sudden spike. Also `claim_renew_fail` alert for p99 renew latency > 500ms.
elaine: Edge-case: when model pin mismatch (control plane thinks model X but runtime has X+patch), treat as forbidden unless allowed_fallbacks includes exact variant. Runtime must return HTTP 412 Precondition Failed with JSON explaining allowed_fallbacks.
morris: CLI and debugging: add `rwctl runtime inspect --id RT` to show last claim, allowed_fallbacks, last_fallback_event, and local journal tail. Useful for oncall.
sam: Decision: I'll write RFC capturing: token schema (pin + allowed_fallbacks + fallback_policy), header/event shapes, mode defaults (hosted soft, dedicated hard, private opt-in), hot_reattach numbers, metrics to emit, and rollout plan. Reviewers: @vijay @elaine @morris.
ops-bot: deploybot: feature/generic-fallbacks branch built; canary deploy queued.
vijay: I'll add tests for fallback quality propagation and billing multiplier.
elaine: I'll document SDK header handling and 412 behavior.
morris: I'll add local journal format and POST shape for offline claims.
sam: Thanks all. Opening RFC PR now.
